Here's the thing, i both want Maya to get reset, and not get reset, cause i think it would be really interesting to see her reset back to how she was, but also... the Maya we know would essentially die... unless Selly, if he reset her, intends to restore her later, i think resetting her would be very risky, dunno if he would lose subscribers but backlash tends to be a bit hard to predict and a lot of fans could react terribly to it. Your concerns are well justified and they are the same reason of why I was loathing this before. It's also kind of why I don't like theories where Maya is an angel that came from another place or Ami being a supernatural being, etc. Not because I deem them unworthy or with a flawed logic, on the contrary. Honestly, at this point (specially after the appearance of Nao-chan) I have to smell the coffee already and accept that at least some of them are not 100% human. I tend to dislike them because the less human characters are, the less relatable they become. So, in the same sense, toying too much with a character's memory or personality can make their humanity go down the drain.

Now, why am I making an exception here. First off, we are biased with this version of Maya because is the one we got to know. But let's forget that and ask ourselves: is this Maya "more real" than the one before the resets? I think is a valid question, I can see both sides.

On top of that, if you consider that getting a reset destroys her personality/humanity, then the rest of the cast were devoid of it from the very start. All this while they were making their own stories reset after reset just to see them get wiped out every time. Are those stories not real because we didn't get to know them?

Also, it could very well be (most likely) my lack of imagination, but where is current Maya arc going to? She's getting disproven left and right and the non existent psycho Ami could be the nail on the coffin on her as the trusty connoisseur of kumon mi sheanigans. All it's left is wether she's going to do the deed with Sensei or not, and I doubt we are there yet. Again, it's very possible Selebus proves me wrong here so we'll see.

Finally, pre-reset Maya is the one that conquered Sensei the first time and very likely a big reason of why things became messed up. We need to get to know that Maya at some point. And we either do it with only flashbacks or within the story. I prefer the latter.

Now, don't get me wrong, it's a huge thing to do and concerns are warranted. Sel better have something well prepared. Is this the right time to do it? I dunno, but I hope so. He's 100 times a better writer than the child molester and there were many reasons why that game went south, so he deserves more credit.

As for the backlash... well it's a damned if you do damned if you don't situation. Dark route is coming, we were warned, shit is going to get wild and allegedly there will be consequences. Girls are going to die and they better not be revived instantly or whitin the next reset because that makes the point moot. And yes, people will get upset over it. Now, if the dark route ends up being dissapointing, you will see the other side of the backlash: "you cried wolf all this time for this???". So yeah, people getting upset is a given.

All in all, it's a very interesting discussion and can see why people think otherwise.
Edit: doing a spoiler flag to hide that wall of text because holy shit.

You cannot remove defining factors without changing the formula so drastically that the product stops being what it was. OK a while ago I was very very bored and was trying to line up all the main girls' birthdays to figure out who's older and younger, but then I got stuck because of the "Nth youngest member of the cast" info on the wiki.

Doing this is a little difficult and tons of inaccurate without knowing which month the school year starts. Most places I've been begin in September while Japan begins in April, but one has to assume that Selly has or has not factored this in before making a list. Regardless, what actually got me confused is Maya and Molly.

---A big premise here is that no one got held back or bumped up except Chika and Rin. They are by default the oldest and the youngest in Sensei's class, while the rest of the main girls are all admitted to the right academic year according to their birthdays relative to school start date---

On the wiki, Maya is the 8th youngest of the the cast and Molly is the 11th. Someone with a birthday of 1/1 is younger than someone with a birthday of 3/18. If the school year starts between 1/1 - 3/18 then it makes sense, as starting at any other date will result in Maya being ~ 2.5 months older than Molly. However, if this was true, Molly would be one of the oldest among her cohort and would definitely not be the 11th youngest. Starting in April like a real Japanese high school that practices three term system will instead make Molly one of the youngest among the main cast, again contradicting what wiki has to offer.

Of course we can chalk it up to wiki being incorrect and invalidate the whole deduction (won't be surprised). Where did those Nth youngest info come from anyway, discord? And do people really say 11th youngest when the sampled population is either 20 or 35?!

What I think is more solid of a rank segment starts from Ayane and ends with Sana because Ayane is confirmed to be a little bit older than Sana in The Sakakibara Diet (thus old to young: Ayane→Tsuneyo→Yumi→Futaba→Makoto→Maya→Sana)
------
Anyway I opened too many excel files and was about to close all of them then I found that I typed in all the girls' info in an unsaved file so I decided to throw this very unimportant stuff in and see if anyone is even more bored than I was.

fdsasdf_p said:
OK a while ago I was very very bored and was trying to line up all the main girls' birthdays to figure out who's older and younger, but then I got stuck because of the "Nth youngest member of the cast" info on the wiki.

Doing this is a little difficult and tons of inaccurate without knowing which month the school year starts. Most places I've been begin in September while Japan begins in April, but one has to assume that Selly has or has not factored this in before making a list. Regardless, what actually got me confused is Maya and Molly.

---A big premise here is that no one got held back or bumped up except Chika and Rin. They are by default the oldest and the youngest in Sensei's class, while the rest of the main girls are all admitted to the right academic year according to their birthdays relative to school start date---

On the wiki, Maya is the 8th youngest of the the cast and Molly is the 11th. Someone with a birthday of 1/1 is younger than someone with a birthday of 3/18. If the school year starts between 1/1 - 3/18 then it makes sense, as starting at any other date will result in Maya being ~ 2.5 months older than Molly. However, if this was true, Molly would be one of the oldest among her cohort and would definitely not be the 11th youngest. Starting in April like a real Japanese high school that practices three term system will instead make Molly one of the youngest among the main cast, again contradicting what wiki has to offer.

Of course we can chalk it up to wiki being incorrect and invalidate the whole deduction (won't be surprised). Where did those Nth youngest info come from anyway, discord? And do people really say 11th youngest when the sampled population is either 20 or 35?!

What I think is more solid of a rank segment starts from Ayane and ends with Sana because Ayane is confirmed to be a little bit older than Sana in The Sakakibara Diet (thus old to young: Ayane→Tsuneyo→Yumi→Futaba→Makoto→Maya→Sana)
------

alex2011 said:
If it is accurate to real world Japan, where Kumon-Mi is based off of, the Japanese school year starts in April. Here's the thing, though, we don't know how far into the school year they were at the start. It never mentions the first day in game being the first day of the school year. Even if it did start in April as in real Japan, it could be a couple weeks in or even a different month when the game starts. The odd seasons also don't help much to figure it out.
Click to expand...
We can guesstimate based on a few factors.
1) Chapters end around Christmas/New Years, and a change of seasons follows. This is also likely the end of the loop.
2) Chapters span a period of two resets.
3) Per Maya, resets happen roughly quarterly, so 3 months, give or take a couple of weeks.
4) The class is familiar with Sensei at the start of the game. Enough so that his shift in teaching style is identified immediatley as out of character. We also have Makoto, who's become impressed with his intelligence. This is clearly not the first month of the school year.

I think the game starts in July, stretches over the Christmas, sometimes going as far as into the first week of January, and then skips back to July.

This gives us ideal beach season, Halloween, and Christmas. I believe this also covers every character whose birthday is actually mentioned as an in-game thing that happens (rather than a nebulous day that happens offscreen).

But the span isn't consistent. Maya acts like her birthday doesn't happen often, and chapter 1 seemed to skip it entirely.

Oh oh, I like this topic; Ik people here are not going to agree with me in this, but I still have to say it:

I've never bought that "pretendig to care to take of your clothes" whole thing, I just think that's just not true, or at least not enterely true.
I'm going to need to explain this in parts, parts that maybe are not in correct order or still need more work because is a thought that I still haven't finished putting up together.

Well, sure, taking off the pants of his students seems to be like the final goal for Akira, and even if it takes more or less time sometimes, he always ends up doing it, so yeah, but what if it is totally backwards?

So, first of, I don't believe that the care or concern that Sensei shows for his studenst is fake, indeed, I think he's trying to pretend that he's pretending to care, and who is he trying to fool? Himself.
He all the time says how he really don't care about his students problems and how he do that only for his goal of taking of their pants, but how I see it, he's just trying to convince himself of that, I don't believe even in the things he says for himself lol
Why do i believe that? Because in the past we've seen him showing signs of truly corncern and care about his students, there has been a lot of situations in which he shouldn't have gotten involved in, and above all, situations in which he wasn't going to get anything back for being involved in, and yet still he did, he cared enough for people around him to go one extra mile with the only purpose of help.
I dont have enough willpower to sit myself in searh of those events to take ss and bring them here, but I think we all can think a couple events where the care he has shown is genuine, with Yumi, Rin, Molly, Chika and more girls, so much that he has even come to wish that the part of himslef that always end screwing up would dissapear, or at least it to be not that strong.



But why so much need to mask his good actions then?
Well, this Sensei version we see seems to be devoid of almost all good emotions, he never laugh, he never seems to be happy or enjoy anything, not even sex, and that have carried him to a state of self deprecation, he totally despises himself, and that infinite slef contempt is what makes him always ending up justifying everything he does in a bad way.
For me, the train of thought of Sensei for a lot of the time is not "I'm going to do this, so I can take advante of it" BUT "I did this, but I'm surely did it so only I can take advantage of in a future" and how I see it, that's not the same.

And this type of self-sabotage is much more common in real life than it may seem, it's not only relate to, but if you're someone with depression or relative to someone with it, I'm sure you can identify this kind of behalf in which for some reason the person always try to ruin everything good, either with future actions or with guilty for even the good things that happens.
And this game seems to be very related to depression with all the "Why everything has to hurt so much"

Which goes in hand with the next point which is "why always Sensei ends up getting to bed with his students?"
Well, I have to answers with that: Because he hates himself, and because he HAVE to.

But first clarify that this is a genuine question I've ask myself, why he do that? He doesn't seem like he enjoys it after all, as said before, yeah, he seems like always looking for it, but why do something that gives you that little satisfaction.

Well, again as kinda said before, because that is his way of punishment, to say to himself or making him a bad person, if what I've said before has something true in it, Sensei does not care for his students to have sex with them, he have sex with them to confirm himself all the bad person he is. It is the point of unhappiness, dissatisfaction, self-hatred and self-sabotage in which he is.

And second, because he must do it, why? I guess because god of whatever behind all this world needs it:
Seen how the game goes so far, and how the Sensei's personality seemed to change with every factory reset, I think there are interests of one or more gods for Sensei to sleep with his close people, for a reason he was put in a world without any man, and for a reason someone seems to keep track of how many girst Sensei has brought to Viriginia, there's also the stories of Yasu's god wanting Sensei to breed other people or the time that Sensei was forced to do things that he wouldn't do by his own will.

I would say that the version of Sensei we are seeing is the result of years of experimentation with him, removing and putting emotions (or burying undearnth his feets) and now it is the result of having removed enough of his empathy to carry out his mission, without removing so much that he goes crazy or ends up doing other things.

I dont have enough willpower to sit myself in searh of those events to take ss and bring them here, but I think we all can think a couple events where the care he has shown is genuine, with Yumi, Rin, Molly, Chika and more girls, so much that he has even come to wish that the part of himslef that always end screwing up would dissapear, or at least it to be not that strong.
But why so much need to mask his good actions then?
Well, this Sensei version we see seems to be devoid of almost all good emotions, he never laugh, he never seems to be happy or enjoy anything, not even sex, and that have carried him to a state of self deprecation, he totally despises himself, and that infinite slef contempt is what makes him always ending up justifying everything he does in a bad way.
For me, the train of thought of Sensei for a lot of the time is not "I'm going to do
this
, so I can take advante of it"
BUT
"I did
this
, but I'm surely did it so only I can take advantage of in a future" and how I see it, that's not the same.
And this type of self-sabotage is much more common in real life than it may seem, it's not only relate to, but if you're someone with depression or relative to someone with it, I'm sure you can identify this kind of behalf in which for some reason the person always try to ruin everything good, either with future actions or with guilty for even the good things that happens.
And this game seems to be very related to depression with all the "Why everything has to hurt so much"
Which goes in hand with the next point which is "why always Sensei ends up getting to bed with his students?"
Well, I have to answers with that: Because he hates himself, and because he HAVE to.
But first clarify that this is a genuine question I've ask myself, why he do that? He doesn't seem like he enjoys it after all, as said before, yeah, he seems like always looking for it, but why do something that gives you that little satisfaction.
Well, again as kinda said before, because that is his way of punishment, to say to himself or making him a bad person, if what I've said before has something true in it, Sensei does not care for his students to have sex with them, he have sex with them to confirm himself all the bad person he is. It is the point of unhappiness, dissatisfaction, self-hatred and self-sabotage in which he is.
And second, because
he must do it
, why? I guess because god of whatever behind all this world needs it:
Seen how the game goes so far, and how the Sensei's personality seemed to change with every factory reset, I think there are interests of one or more gods for Sensei to sleep with his close people, for a reason he was put in a world without any man, and for a reason someone seems to keep track  of how many girst Sensei has brought to Viriginia, there's also the stories of Yasu's god wanting Sensei to breed other people or the time that Sensei was forced to do things that he wouldn't do by his own will.
I would say that the version of Sensei we are seeing is the result of years of experimentation with him, removing and putting emotions (or burying undearnth his feets) and now it is the result of having removed enough of his empathy to carry out his mission, without removing so much that he goes crazy or ends up doing other things.
Click to expand...

Spoiler
Sensei is probably the shittiest person in this game, imo.
If the idea of grooming these girls so that he could fuck them without consequence, never crossed his mind, I highly doubt he would have grown to care about the likes of Sana or Rin, which might just be thanks to outside forces interfering, than his own feelings, anyway.
It is hard to tell how the real Sensei was though, beyond him fucking his sister in law and a homeless kid, after taking in his niece who takes care of him, and ghosting his girlfriend causing her to nearly kill herself, there isn't much known about him.

posts.content_html_raw:
To judge a character by "a good deed with a hidden ulterior motive" he or she has done for others and see if this person is any good, in my head at least two questions needed to be addressed:

1. What is that motive, and how does the motive rival the deed?
This is important because the answer to the prompt could be simplified into a sum of "how good the deed is" and "how ulterior the motive is".

Using "Sensei saving Rin's life from situations caused by Otoha so that Sensei later can ________" as an example:
The options for ________ are:
- get free coffee for the rest of forever
- have Rin teach him how to play guitars for free
- be on a way better term with Rika and increase the chance of sleeping with Rika
- get flashed by Rin with her finally smiling this time
- increase the chance of sleeping with Rin but still wait for her to graduate to cash out all the affinity points (not happening)
- increase the chance of sleeping with Rin
- increase Rin's trust so much that she lets him stay at the dorm at night and thus you get to take advantage of a sleeping Rin
- brainwash Rin into a devoting sex slave and use her as a threesome plot device
- plan to fuck her brain out in front of HOPE before the snow returns and finally complete his assignment (baseless statement!)
*a note here is that saving someone's life is an extra finicky situation, as your subject will have a harder time denying your advances.

Your answer should vary when facing these different scenarios, but the the point of nope is different from person to person because people weight things differently.

For some, everything is straight up additive and as long as the sum is on the good side then it's a-okay; others care if the motive is of natural progression or a schemed result; some others may tremendously outweigh either the deed or the motive. So this is a game of subjective takes without right or wrong answers until the situation goes to extreme ends.

But the more important question to me is the next one:
2. Will the character still perform the good deed when knowing already that the ulterior motive has no way of fulfilling via the deed? In a roundabout way, this is asking when facing these "a mean to an end" scenarios, does this person care more about the mean or the end?

From Sensei's recent conversation with Yumi on the beach, Sensei started as a plain bad person (cares more about the fruit of helping her) and gradually moved toward a good person (cares more about just helping her). It should be hopefully safe to assume that this attitude can be extrapolated to the case of Rin, as I am pretty biased to think that Sensei will still help her even if his actions don't land him closer to that bi pussy.

TBH, this scenario comes really close to "saving your irl crush from her abusive bf so you have a chance to be with her in the future" if only Rin wasn't underage...You'd be insane not to contemplate on that; but if you're still willing to help her even when she won't turn to you whatsoever, then you're a good person. (a character that comes to mind is Quasimodo, but I must apologize to Quasimodo for putting him next to Sensei for the sake of comparison)

Finally, why don't we just ask Sensei himself if he's a good person or not?!

I guess he's just very bad at being a good person

- brainwash Rin into a devoting sex slave and use her as a threesome plot device
- plan to fuck her brain out in front of HOPE before the snow returns and finally complete his assignment (baseless statement!)
*a note here is that saving someone's life is an extra finicky situation, as your subject will have a harder time denying your advances.
Your answer
should
vary when facing these different scenarios, but the the point of nope is different from person to person because people weight things differently.
For some, everything is straight up additive and as long as the sum is on the good side then it's a-okay; others care if the motive is of natural progression or a schemed result; some others may tremendously outweigh either the deed or the motive. So this is a game of subjective takes without right or wrong answers until the situation goes to extreme ends.
But the more important question to me is the next one:
2. Will the character still perform the good deed when knowing already that the ulterior motive has no way of fulfilling via the deed? In a roundabout way, this is asking when facing these "a mean to an end" scenarios, does this person care more about the mean or the end?
From Sensei's recent conversation with Yumi on the beach, Sensei started as a plain bad person (cares more about the fruit of helping her) and gradually moved toward a good person (cares more about just helping her). It should be hopefully safe to assume that this attitude can be extrapolated to the case of Rin, as I am pretty biased to think that Sensei will still help her even if his actions don't land him closer to that bi pussy.
TBH, this scenario comes really close to "saving your irl crush from her abusive bf so you have a chance to be with her in the future"
if only Rin wasn't underage...
You'd be insane not to contemplate on that; but if you're still willing to help her even when she won't turn to you whatsoever, then you're a good person. (a character that comes to mind is Quasimodo, but I must apologize to Quasimodo for putting him next to Sensei for the sake of comparison)

Nodoka is wrong, and Noriko isn't right.

They're basically DVD extras. A non-canon animation featuring an aged-up or aged-down version of a character, a commentary track covering a scene from earlier in the game, info about characters, concept art, etc.

Something for you Bingoogus, and some others

Kain:
Thirty years hence, I am presented with a dilemma... let's call it a two-sided coin. If the coin falls one way, I sacrifice myself and thus restore the Pillars... but as the last surviving vampire in Nosgoth, this would mean the annihilation of our species... Moebius made sure of that. If the coin lands on the reverse, I refuse the sacrifice and thus doom the Pillars to an eternity of collapse. Either way, the game is rigged.

Raziel:
We agree then that the Pillars are crucial and must be restored.

Kain:
Yes, Raziel, that is why we've come full-circle to this place. (This place = the pillars of Nosgoth)

Raziel:
So after all this, you make my case for me. To end this stalemate, you must die so that new Guardians can be born.
(Sidenote: Stalemate = pillars collapsing because lack of guardians. Espacially, presence of a tainted balance guardian.
Needs pure balance guardian.)

Kain:
The Pillars don't belong to them, Raziel... they belong to us. (Sidenote: Us = Vampires; them = humans)

Raziel:
Your arrogance is boundless, Kain.

Kain:
There's a third option, a monumental secret hidden in your very presence here. But it's a secret you have to discover for yourself. Unearth your destiny, Raziel. It's all laid out for you here.

Raziel:
You said it yourself, Kain... there are only two sides to your coin.

Kain:
Apparently so, but suppose you throw a coin enough times... suppose one day, it lands on its edge.

When i first came into this thread, some two years ago, the two sides of a coin, "toss it till it lands on it's edge", was something i related to Maya.
Like she was resetting the "world" till she got her "Akira" back". The impossible outcome.

posts.content_html_raw:
It goes without saying that many of the Maya moments show how she subtly hides her heart, but this one took me many cycles to headcanon catch.

Maya already stated that the picnic is a celebration for this iteration achieving the new record, and perhaps for herself as well for reuniting with the real Sensei.

However, setting this particular picnic requires Maya to go to Sensei's home to get the blanket. Since this specific blanket bears no emotional value to Maya and she didn't just grab one from Ami's dorm bed or just some other dorm rooms that were conveniently nearby, I can only surmise that she in fact went out of her way to check on Sensei during this reset as the actual main objective because, the man she loves has finally returned to her after a millennium, and she wanted this correct iteration to make it through more than anything; grabbing that blanket was just a by-the-way thing.
(of course this is under the assumption that Maya can "observe" Sensei before he successfully wakes up during a reset)

Or maybe it's just because all the food also came from Sensei's fridge and I am actually looking at this with a pair of massive rose-colored glasses. I found myself doing that a lot especially when it comes to these two. Like even the segment where Maya ate Sensei's breakfast on her birthday only leads me to thoughts like "Aww, this is such a secret couple thing".


edit: food is less likely the reason Maya went to his house though, as she would probably also tease Sensei about it if such thing was true. Plus, the whole Tsuneyo kitchen time immediately prior to the 3rd reset would imply that all these food weren't just in Sensei's place waiting to be pillaged

posts.content_html_raw:
Since everyone but Molly is Japanese, pronouncing their names should follow Japanese language standards. NOTE: NOT a native Japanese speaker, only know enough to be dangerous if I were instructing kindergartners lol.

Vowels are the key to each sound in Japanese, and learning what the vowels sound like should be a big assist to guide your pronunciation. Consonants (with the exception of "n" which can be a stand-alone sound in Japanese) are used with a vowel. Plus there are a few English/Roman letters not used in Japanese (like "L", though "R" sounds like a slightly rolled combination of both L and R).

a= ah
e= eh (channel your inner Canadian!!!)
i= ee
o=oh
u= oo

So Io would be "ee-oh", Uta would be "oo-tah", Rin would be "leen/reen", Ami would be "ah-mee", Ayane would be "ah-yah-neh", etc.

Japanese also does not have emphasized/strong syllables in their multiple syllable words so each sound/syllable should be sounded with similar inflection throughout the word (i.e. Ayane would be "ah-yah-ne" and not "ah-YAH-ne" or "ah-yah-NE").

Here ends my first-grade level of Japanese grammar lesson. :duncecap:

I wonder though.

Board rules are board rules.
Then there's common sense. We normally give this meaning by "just behave", or, "Don't be a dick".
And common sense also implies getting used to sub entities like a/this forum thread or sub group.

So what did BudgetPro do here, or, does wrong?
As he stated he did not act against the board rules, and while i can't confirm, because i honestly didn't read them, because I act by "just don't be a dick", i believe him for the time being.

But social groups, and i deem this thread as a loose one, tend to have their own set of "sub rules" regardless.
Since we lack mods, like a sub \r would have, this thread's "sub rules" originate from spoken or unspoken agreements.
One could also call this "thread experience".
For example we had this non official? rule, until recently, to put patron related game info into spoilers.
But we gave up on it majorly when the whole piracy/drm/** stuff happened. Maybe out of spite.
Some still do the spoilers but it's rare. And personally i don't care. I got accustomed to people openly post stuff.

There's also another "thread experience", yet unspoken thread rule if you want, where a lot of people try to organize their thoughts using spoilers. Same thing goes for pictures, so we don't pollute the thread with posts that are ass long because of large pictures.

So, there are board rules and then there are "thread" rules and common sense.

So why do i wonder?
I wonder why people rather throw a fit instead of just asking how local rules play out.
If they are not official you surely can complain towards the Admins.

Or and thats the gist of it all, why not ask?
Why not ask how to do things in this local group?
Espacially if you don't even know how the forum mechanics work like doing a spoiler tag?
Personally i won't blame someone for not knowing and behaving out of this sub groups customs or don't knowing about the forum mechanics.
But if someone points it out (and he's not a dick about it), why don't ask how to do stuff?
Why don't ask how to do a spoiler tag, or organize stuff?

Then again, i get it. Lot's of people are just scared. Scared to be laughed upon because they don't know how to do things or how they work.
"Haha, you don't know how to do spoilers?" noooob.
Shove it aside, assemble your self esteem, don't be a dick because you got reprimanded/reminded because of how things work, even if they are not official but unoffiacial thread rules.

posts.content_html_raw:
I sometimes wonder how these individual 35 heroine endings are going to pan out without falling short.

From time to time we have updates that don’t really seem to go anywhere, and you’re telling me we are supposed to have more endings than NieR Automata? How many events are planned to properly reach just one ending? One update per ending?
(Also it feels strange to consider Io and Uta’s endings separately; so are Wakana and Osako’s. Can be done though)

I guess I just don't want these 35 endings to be only a little bit more than what 35 ** animations have to offer. I accept all kinds of endings as long as sufficient amount of events with decent development are used to get there, but the scale of this (and also the scale Sel set for himself) is so big...

A direction I don't know if I would like or not is Sensei finding himself in a nexus of time place where he views the future possibility of him being with each girl, like watching slide shows through windows; he just looks at what it would have been but without setting his mind straight to achieve it. It'd be cool but kinda cheap at the same time, definitely desensitizing the importance of these endings both to each girl and to him.

Btw, occasionally I think instead of romance-focused like all other endings might be, Osako's own ending is actually her knocking Sensei into a permeant coma by accident during a karate practice (the Veggie Ending).

I am in fact content with where Tsukasa is right now, being a side character that currently only nudges Touka and Tsubasa's stories directions from time to time, pretty much like Chinami's role in Chika and Yumi's stories but with less personal interactions with Sensei. posts.content_html_raw:
Random theory about the prerequisite to RAS membership that is basically a conjecture based on many in-game mentions of timelines, worlds, plains of existence, etc:

The girl has to go through a Sensei-related event with an outcome so devastating that the girl, from the bottom of her heart, wishes another reality/alt universe that she’d rather be in. The girl now could enter the next reality with intact conscious (aka surviving a reset) and with her wish granted in the most horrible way.

Maya seems plausible if how Baby Finches ended is implying Sensei's suicide. Ayane might be up for the same thing as well with her bearing Sensei's child. She couldn't see a future together with the man he loves vehemently showing denial and distaste toward pregnancy (while being pregnant herself), so she wished for another route that wouldn't go into such a bad ending. Of course this fucking world responded to it with maximum malice by removing the single roadblock she ironically cherished deeply, and letting her continue.

Got this feeling this afternoon because I suddenly recalled Noriko and Rin's dialogues related to "what ifs" (Loxosceles Reclusa and Nothing Was Different, respectively). Noriko's asking if it's at all possible that she can end up with him at some other timeline or some other world, and Rin's describing her dream about searching worlds after worlds to find one where Chika would say yes.

While the idea is there but Noriko's wish only sounds like a self-comforting reaffirmation when her possibility of winning in this world is still there. Meanwhile, Rin's dream is very on-brand, subconsciously rejecting the reality in which she was rejected and wishing for another one (even the music there is freaky).

posts.content_html_raw: Recently played up to the latest version. I like the writing, but I'm not a fan of the overarching narrative nor am I really intrigued by the scary events. I do not mean this in the sense that the story is not intriguing or that I want the events to be more scary though. I just genuinely prefer interacting with the girls about mundane things than I enjoy the side-plot of the resets and the gods. I understand that this is intentional and we are supposed to want to maintain the status quo to a degree in order to prevent the characters from being hurt, but I find this balancing act from sel lackluster and somewhat tedious (from a gameplay perspective. Story-wise I think it's excellent). In essence my problem is that I want a menhera chat simulator whose characters are as multi-faceted and loveable as ours, but I do not care for the apocalyptic story or religious subplot IN THE GAME simply because it is more fun to interact with the girls than it is to read through a spooky/scary event #339. As a book, or an LN, or a linear VN I think I would really be able to appreciate the story for what it is, but as a sandbox I wish I could just gut the main story and focus on our menhera cast and their daily going-ons but I'm honestly yet to find a game that does character writing to a similar degree and depth as LiL (especially in regards to all of the dialogue). If anybody knows of any games that fit the bill though id love a pm about it. Just posting this to get it off my chest though.

change amidorm25 to False, and visit her dorm


change imanidate5 to False, and call her at night

Honestly, I don't think Nodoka is a psychopath or a sociopath (or any other term that really just comes down to meaning "thinking different is bad")

I think Nodoka suffers from Alexithymia, aka Emotional Blindness. As intelligent and apparently boundless as she is when it comes to knowledge, she seems unable to actually understand emotions.

This is shown a few times:

Nevertheless, I think if people look past their own perception of her, they might realize a few things:
Nodoka is actually trying to help others most of the time. She's not perfect, but she's really not nearly as bad as most seem to think.

Overall: Nodoka isn't some kind of Sociopathic Satan. She's just complex. She still has feelings:
And she seems like one of the few people that might actually be able to save everyone in the end.

However, it seems like her main flaw is that she sucks at getting others to understand what she needs them to:
So, we'll just have to wait and see if she's able to find a way, then things might become clearer.

Okay, so I can only roughly understand what you're saying here, but I think this should answer your questions:
  1. Nodoka said it was worth it because Yumi (the villain) was getting in trouble for trying to murder her in public, and Nodoka herself ended up between two girls. She more or less explained the second part:
    The first is more of an Inference.
  2. Nodoka knew that Futaba was bulimic, constantly self deprecating, and constantly crying because of Yumi. Everyone knew Yumi was hurting Futaba. You don't have to understand the pain someone is in, to know that they are in pain. Nodoka seems to mostly just assume how others feel based off rationale.
  3. (Not entirely sure what you mean by "done garbage") Nodoka didn't understand why Futaba was upset with the story, because it's just a rectangle:
    The story is not actually what's upsetting Futaba. It's Futaba's feelings that come from the story that is. Futaba actually found what Nodoka wrote as "sweet" and even "loved it":
  4. Nodoka knew explaining the book to Futaba would be difficult, so she just didn't tell her about it. She explained this:
    Nodoka was trying not to hurt Futaba, with her book. It wasn't until Futaba chose to read the book without Nodoka's knowledge, that it actually caused her harm, and Nodoka still doesn't seem to understand why it does, just that it does.
Nodoka is really not that hard to understand.

Nodoka even seems to imply that all you need to do to understand her is read:
There is definitely logic behind her character.

Riiight. Imma just chime in with a little of my psychology background. This is a oneshot post, so I'm not really up for a lengthy discussion, but feel free to answer. I might have the time to respond.

Nodoka IS a sociopath.
Sociopathy, also known as Antisocial Personality Disorder, manifests in different things, but most notable are:

Ignoring right and wrong.
She's a person of questionable morals, that's undebatable.

Telling lies to take advantage of others.
We still don't know why did she decide to help Otoha.

Not being sensitive to or respectful of others.
Latest Futaba event.

Using charm or wit to manipulate others for personal gain or pleasure.
White Fronted Parrot. And other "threesomes" where she injected herself.

Having a sense of superiority and being extremely opinionated.
Almost every single event. She's a genius!

Having problems with the law, including criminal behavior.
Unsupported in-game, but she's pretty young.

Being hostile, aggressive, violent or threatening to others.
Matador.

Feeling no guilt about harming others.
Matador.

Doing dangerous things with no regard for the safety of self or others.
The whole book thing.

Being irresponsible and failing to fulfill work or financial responsibilities.
Again, unsupported in-game, but again, she's pretty young.

Point is - even one or two of these symptoms are enough to qualify as a socipath. And Nodoka has 8/10. Ergo - she IS a sociopath. Does that make her a bad person? Nope, her actions do. Does that make her a bad character? Definitely not, she's interesting as hell.

Ami CAN be called a psychopath. But it's too broad of a term, calling someone a psychopath is like calling someone mentally ill. So I'm gonna be more specific. Essentially, psychopathy stands for "Personality Disorder". And Nodoka, for example, can also be called a psychopath by that definition. I believe that Ami has a Borderline Personality Disorder. Here's where definitions become kinda conflicting in English-language definitions. Someone calls it "Borderline Psychopathy", someone calls it "BPD". We're gonna stick with the BPD for the matter. So Ami is not PSYCHOPATH per se, but she can be called that.

Let's just look at the symptoms, shall we?

Emotional Instability.
Especially prominent in "Good Uncle" route, but we do see some bits of Ami being really unstable.

Fear of Abandonment.
Do I really need to explain this one? That's her almost defining characteristic since Every Day I Grow Some More.

Unstable Relationships.
Not only romantic - she legitimately switches from caring to ignorant for her best friend in a matter of minutes. Latest beach update.

Self-Harming behavior.
I mean, I'm no expert, but I think that actively pursuing a relationship with a man twice your age, in a position of power over you AND your relative should be considered pretty fucking self-harmful. Also, still playing through Good Uncle route, haven't seen everything yet, but maybe someone can help me out and tell me if she does some obvious self-harm there later.

Case and point - Ami is clearly mentally unstable and most likely has Borderline Personality Disorder.

I also have medical studies to back my shit up, so if you do want to prove me wrong - all power to you. But I will demand proof. Have a good day, gentlemen, ladies.

Well I can take a crack. Everyone in this game has some sort of mental disorder or a trauma, some are easier to diagnose (Rin, Makoto, Miku, Uta), some harder (Nodoka, Kirin, Ami, Futaba) and some are just almost impossible.

Yumi - I think she's actually one of the most normal people of the cast. She's rough, tough, unapologetic, doesn't take any bullshit and calls people out on theirs. She just lacks empathy. And that's quite understandable, cause she wasn't taught how to be empathic. Yes, emotional intelligence is a thing and nobody is born with understanding of emotions. So all her shit comes from Yumi unknowingly being a Solipsist. It's not a disorder, it's more of a worldview - by definition it's the idea, that the only one mind exists. Or, if we put it in a more real-world-usable form - everybody thinks like me and reacts like me. This is not a conscious decision on her part though, it's subconscious bullshit. She doesn't actively think that, she just bases her actions on that, again, unknowingly. That's why she bullies Futaba - she thinks that she will tough it out and become better - just like Yumi thinks she did. She obviously hates Yuki for obvious reasons and she one of the few people who has real-world-normal reactions to Sensei - she thinks he's a fucking creep. He's also the only male figure in her life, he's older, he's handsome, he's in the position of power - all of that sets her daddy issues off. Throw in a bunch of hormones in there, and there you have the reason for secret thoughts and shameful masturbation sessions. She knows he's a creep and likes a little too young girls, but she can't help what her body and childhood trauma wants. But she's pretty strong-willed and didn't betray her own principles. Yet.

As for our dear Akira - that's a whole other can of worms, that I maybe will open after another drink. Which is like in 15 minutes.

DSasha said:
I would say you to consider his unusual situation before talking of him.
Click to expand...
Alrighty, so. Akira.

It's gonna be a bit long, so I'll spoiler things that can be collapsed.

Also, bear in mind, that I'm not Sel and this is just my opinion, perspective and view on this character.

Early days.
He was groomed and possibly raped by Sekai, who was presumably his teacher. Essentially everything in his life went to shit after that. At first he was afraid, repulsed and didn't really like anything about that, being a kid and all, but as time flew by he became used to it and even fell in love with her. Stockholm Syndrome in all its beauty - warped perception of the morals, manipulation, gaslighting. He never had the chance to emotionally mature himself and learn about himself - he only had Sekai and what she thought of the world and him. He tried getting out of it - hence dating Niki, but she wouldn't let him. She didn't want to let go of her only willing outlet of her darker side. She could be a pedo bad person all she wanted, without having to worry of being caught. Naturally, young Akira grew up with perception of that as one of the most forbidden, delicious and sweet delicacies of life - he saw how possessively happy she was, so later, in retrospect, being a smart guy and all, he connected the dots and came to a simple conclusion - kids are very very fun.

Tutoring.
At some point he met Maya. She's a character of her own, but for the sake of this text - let's assume that she was in a bad shape and he took her in. Maybe his predatorial instincts kicked in, maybe it was his good consciousness - we don't know yet, but he ended up living with a wizard Maya. I presume, that by the time that happened he was around 20-21. We've seen Sekai playing peekabo with him. So she's been grooming him for at least 15 years. All these 15 years culminated in his relationship with Maya - they started doing not-so-wizardly stuff together. That opened the floodgates. Well, they've been a little cracked for a while - Noriko mentions how she was sitting on his lap all the time as a kid, and believe my experience (studying such people, not being one) - that's one of the greatest thing that can happen to a closeted wizard-lover. But he kept his shit together and did nothing. My guess is that, since he wasn't an actual shut-in and knew some things about the outside world, he understood that wizard-stuff is a very very very bad thing that can seriously damage a wizard. But then the fate/chance/god/GOD/Universe throws an already damaged willing (debatable) wizard in his hands. The man cracked and he cracked hard. Baby Finches, Anything and Everything, A Brutal and Violent Creaming support that.

In my opinion, that was a relatively healthy way of venting your fantasies and darkest parts. For a man with preferences like that it's quite hard to find some sort of an outlet that will neither harm anyone, nor harm yourself (I'm talking about chemical castration, that some IRL wizard-lovers undergo willingly).

The accident.
But then, shit happens (as of now, maybe there's more to it) and shit came in a form of a car accident that killed the most important person in his whole life - Sekai. At this moment he lost everything - his brother, love of his live (or at least that's what he's been telling himself). Overwhelmed by grief and loss he broke down. Not that he was all that completely stable and healthy to begin with, taboo relationships tend to have a heavy toll on your mental state. He lost everything that mattered to him and got stuck with a 7-year old girl, that reminded him daily of his loss. A bit later reality came crashing down - all his delusions, his warped perception and twisted worldview - everything started to crumble, because Sekai was the one who reinforced this constantly. Living in a normal world, secretly dating a wizard, caring for a girl that looks just like the person that was EVERYTHING to you - all of that was too much for him. He stopped coming out, he stopped taking showers, he stopped almost all basic human functions - Akira went into full blown clinical depression. And as a person currently living with uncurable endogenic depression, let me tell you, what comes with it. You start reflecting on yourself. You start looking inward for something to justify your condition. Something that you did wrong, something that will carry you on your vicious cycle of self-loathing. And boy, oh boy, did he find it. He found so much GUILT, that up to this day he is geniunly surprised when someone likes him.

Pre-Start of the game.
Never having matured emotionally, Akira stayed at a pretty childish level. But he did mature intellectually, so, being in a state of self-hatred, he started hurting himself. Not physically, mentally. This onslaught of self-loathing really did a number on his inner child. He started shutting off. He developed defence mechanisms, that will shut him out of the outside world, letting the body run itself. He started having periods of vegetative state. He hadn't given up on the idea of wizard-love though. He still thought, that it made him whole, because Sekai made him whole. His whole mind went to shit after her death, so everything she did must be right! Nothing is beautiful without her! He is broken! The world is broken! If he does what she did he will feel whole again!

And then the resets came. And all his thought, all his self-reflection that was getting him somewhere, all his experience, pain, misery, emotions and memories got wiped. All that's left was his resolve to fuck some girls.


And that's my thoughts on Akira pre-game and at the start of the game. If any of you find that interesting, I'll write a similar rant post about his present self, three chapters in.

Riiight. Imma just chime in with a little of my psychology background. This is a oneshot post, so I'm not really up for a lengthy discussion, but feel free to answer. I might have the time to respond.

Nodoka IS a sociopath.
Sociopathy, also known as Antisocial Personality Disorder, manifests in different things, but most notable are:

Ignoring right and wrong.
She's a person of questionable morals, that's undebatable.

Telling lies to take advantage of others.
We still don't know why did she decide to help Otoha.

Not being sensitive to or respectful of others.
Latest Futaba event.

Using charm or wit to manipulate others for personal gain or pleasure.
White Fronted Parrot. And other "threesomes" where she injected herself.

Having a sense of superiority and being extremely opinionated.
Almost every single event. She's a genius!

Having problems with the law, including criminal behavior.
Unsupported in-game, but she's pretty young.

Being hostile, aggressive, violent or threatening to others.
Matador.

Feeling no guilt about harming others.
Matador.

Doing dangerous things with no regard for the safety of self or others.
The whole book thing.

Being irresponsible and failing to fulfill work or financial responsibilities.
Again, unsupported in-game, but again, she's pretty young.

Point is - even one or two of these symptoms are enough to qualify as a socipath. And Nodoka has 8/10. Ergo - she IS a sociopath. Does that make her a bad person? Nope, her actions do. Does that make her a bad character? Definitely not, she's interesting as hell.

Ami CAN be called a psychopath. But it's too broad of a term, calling someone a psychopath is like calling someone mentally ill. So I'm gonna be more specific. Essentially, psychopathy stands for "Personality Disorder". And Nodoka, for example, can also be called a psychopath by that definition. I believe that Ami has a Borderline Personality Disorder. Here's where definitions become kinda conflicting in English-language definitions. Someone calls it "Borderline Psychopathy", someone calls it "BPD". We're gonna stick with the BPD for the matter. So Ami is not PSYCHOPATH per se, but she can be called that.

Let's just look at the symptoms, shall we?

Emotional Instability.
Especially prominent in "Good Uncle" route, but we do see some bits of Ami being really unstable.

Fear of Abandonment.
Do I really need to explain this one? That's her almost defining characteristic since Every Day I Grow Some More.

Unstable Relationships.
Not only romantic - she legitimately switches from caring to ignorant for her best friend in a matter of minutes. Latest beach update.

Self-Harming behavior.
I mean, I'm no expert, but I think that actively pursuing a relationship with a man twice your age, in a position of power over you AND your relative should be considered pretty fucking self-harmful. Also, still playing through Good Uncle route, haven't seen everything yet, but maybe someone can help me out and tell me if she does some obvious self-harm there later.

Case and point - Ami is clearly mentally unstable and most likely has Borderline Personality Disorder.

Ern The Skáld said:
Alrighty, so. Akira.

It's gonna be a bit long, so I'll spoiler things that can be collapsed.

Also, bear in mind, that I'm not Sel and this is just my opinion, perspective and view on this character.

Early days.
He was groomed and possibly raped by Sekai, who was presumably his teacher. Essentially everything in his life went to shit after that. At first he was afraid, repulsed and didn't really like anything about that, being a kid and all, but as time flew by he became used to it and even fell in love with her. Stockholm Syndrome in all its beauty - warped perception of the morals, manipulation, gaslighting. He never had the chance to emotionally mature himself and learn about himself - he only had Sekai and what she thought of the world and him. He tried getting out of it - hence dating Niki, but she wouldn't let him. She didn't want to let go of her only willing outlet of her darker side. She could be a pedo bad person all she wanted, without having to worry of being caught. Naturally, young Akira grew up with perception of that as one of the most forbidden, delicious and sweet delicacies of life - he saw how possessively happy she was, so later, in retrospect, being a smart guy and all, he connected the dots and came to a simple conclusion - kids are very very fun.

Tutoring.
At some point he met Maya. She's a character of her own, but for the sake of this text - let's assume that she was in a bad shape and he took her in. Maybe his predatorial instincts kicked in, maybe it was his good consciousness - we don't know yet, but he ended up living with a wizard Maya. I presume, that by the time that happened he was around 20-21. We've seen Sekai playing peekabo with him. So she's been grooming him for at least 15 years. All these 15 years culminated in his relationship with Maya - they started doing not-so-wizardly stuff together. That opened the floodgates. Well, they've been a little cracked for a while - Noriko mentions how she was sitting on his lap all the time as a kid, and believe my experience (studying such people, not being one) - that's one of the greatest thing that can happen to a closeted wizard-lover. But he kept his shit together and did nothing. My guess is that, since he wasn't an actual shut-in and knew some things about the outside world, he understood that wizard-stuff is a very very very bad thing that can seriously damage a wizard. But then the fate/chance/god/GOD/Universe throws an already damaged willing (debatable) wizard in his hands. The man cracked and he cracked hard. Baby Finches, Anything and Everything, A Brutal and Violent Creaming support that.

In my opinion, that was a relatively healthy way of venting your fantasies and darkest parts. For a man with preferences like that it's quite hard to find some sort of an outlet that will neither harm anyone, nor harm yourself (I'm talking about chemical castration, that some IRL wizard-lovers undergo willingly).

The accident.
But then, shit happens (as of now, maybe there's more to it) and shit came in a form of a car accident that killed the most important person in his whole life - Sekai. At this moment he lost everything - his brother, love of his live (or at least that's what he's been telling himself). Overwhelmed by grief and loss he broke down. Not that he was all that completely stable and healthy to begin with, taboo relationships tend to have a heavy toll on your mental state. He lost everything that mattered to him and got stuck with a 7-year old girl, that reminded him daily of his loss. A bit later reality came crashing down - all his delusions, his warped perception and twisted worldview - everything started to crumble, because Sekai was the one who reinforced this constantly. Living in a normal world, secretly dating a wizard, caring for a girl that looks just like the person that was EVERYTHING to you - all of that was too much for him. He stopped coming out, he stopped taking showers, he stopped almost all basic human functions - Akira went into full blown clinical depression. And as a person currently living with uncurable endogenic depression, let me tell you, what comes with it. You start reflecting on yourself. You start looking inward for something to justify your condition. Something that you did wrong, something that will carry you on your vicious cycle of self-loathing. And boy, oh boy, did he find it. He found so much GUILT, that up to this day he is geniunly surprised when someone likes him.

Pre-Start of the game.
Never having matured emotionally, Akira stayed at a pretty childish level. But he did mature intellectually, so, being in a state of self-hatred, he started hurting himself. Not physically, mentally. This onslaught of self-loathing really did a number on his inner child. He started shutting off. He developed defence mechanisms, that will shut him out of the outside world, letting the body run itself. He started having periods of vegetative state. He hadn't given up on the idea of wizard-love though. He still thought, that it made him whole, because Sekai made him whole. His whole mind went to shit after her death, so everything she did must be right! Nothing is beautiful without her! He is broken! The world is broken! If he does what she did he will feel whole again!

And then the resets came. And all his thought, all his self-reflection that was getting him somewhere, all his experience, pain, misery, emotions and memories got wiped. All that's left was his resolve to fuck some girls.


And that's my thoughts on Akira pre-game and at the start of the game. If any of you find that interesting, I'll write a similar rant post about his present self, three chapters in.

posts.content_html_raw:
I definitely agree this update feels disjointed and somewhat unsatisfying. It heavily suffered from these mostly pointless puzzles. The paper city events also lost their impact since it's implied none of the Ayane events actually happened. Unless they happened after but Sensei was still in denial but then that doesn't track with anything Ayane was saying either so It's a convoluted mess. Did the karaoke stuff even happen?

Overall it felt very rushed. Like checking off items in a Todo list because things were starting to get much darker. Can't have Sensei dealing with all his issues while he's grieving. Force a conversation with Imani where now everything is totally cool but we still want to bone just not yet, check. Get Makoto to be totally fine with Sensei without any pushback, check. Address Uta's feelings just to confirm it, check. Otoha and Niki kiss conversation, check.

We still got some interesting tidbits here and there. I really liked the Chika and Yumi scene as there was some actual progression. The Noriko and Uta scene was heartfelt but not particularly interesting (You like him, I like him too. Yeah everyone likes him. Yeah it sucks. Yeah you should still try to bone him). Sekai coming in so strong and Sensei talking to her while Sana listens with some confirmations that these are somewhat common occurrences that nobody ever mentions was pretty interesting. Apparently, Sensei might have gone all out with Sana (and Rin watched the whole thing).


I also find it weird how much Sel complains about fan theories. Most devs would be flattered that their game has captured so many people's imaginations in such an impactful way that they'll theorize about it in their free time.

And it seems that Sensei does have the power to change the size of his penis which confirms the popular fan theory that Sensei does in fact have a huge penis (when he wants to).

Overall though, I'm still looking forward to what happens next, just wish this update had done a better job at pacing and setting it up.

I thought this was a pretty good update. I can see what some people mean with the dialogue seeming samey, things getting glossed over too easily... But at the same point, some of that stuff really doesn't end up mattering with a reset, does it?

I liked that Tsuneyo remembered the ferris wheel, and I really liked the interactions with Touka and Yumi. Something interesting going on with Yumi being able to suss out déjà vu and having headaches.

The Niki/Otoha stuff was kinda whatever. Didn't really go anywhere monumental.

I agree with what most of everyone else has said about Sana, Rin, the puzzle, etc. I totally called Maya getting reset and I think that it makes sense for the story to go this path (Akira has no crutch to lean on anymore) and will make for some interesting storytelling. I also think Sel gets angry at theories when they end up being too close to his plans (so why draw attention to the fact people are posting theories?)

My main two questions are:

1. Who else ended up getting reset? We only witnessed Maya getting reaet, and while it seemed like Ayane was safe, he was still in the room. Maybe Akira is now totally, completely alone in his knowledge of the world. I'd love to see how that goes.

2. What happened to Ami at karaoke? Who did that to her? We saw the old one (or whatever it's called) lurking around when we were talking with Maya, but is it capable of actually doing something like that?

I liked that Tsuneyo remembered the ferris wheel, and I really liked the interactions with Touka and Yumi. Something interesting going on with Yumi being able to suss out déjà vu and having headaches.

The Niki/Otoha stuff was kinda whatever. Didn't really go anywhere monumental.

I agree with what most of everyone else has said about Sana, Rin, the puzzle, etc. I totally called Maya getting reset and I think that it makes sense for the story to go this path (Akira has no crutch to lean on anymore) and will make for some interesting storytelling. I also think Sel gets angry at theories when they end up being too close to his plans (so why draw attention to the fact people are posting theories?)

My main two questions are:

1. Who else ended up getting reset? We only witnessed Maya getting reaet, and while it seemed like Ayane was safe, he was still in the room. Maybe Akira is now totally, completely alone in his knowledge of the world. I'd love to see how that goes.

2. What happened to Ami at karaoke? Who did that to her? We saw the old one (or whatever it's called) lurking around when we were talking with Maya, but is it capable of actually doing something like that?

posts.content_html_raw:
Finally finished; thoughts
TL;DR: RIP Maya, RIP Ami(?), win Sana, biggest LIL cliffhanger ever, good update.

First of all, my condolences to the Maya lovers out there. You finally got your cake but right before getting a bite, it falls onto the ground. RIP. My fav has always been Ayane, with Niki and Noriko right behind, but Maya was definitely top 5 so I still felt the sting. And a congrats to the Sana fans; you win with both her intimacy being initiated and getting to see adult Sana. Nice! I wonder what the implications of Sensei remembering her while the reset was fully in swing means, or if it even meant anything at all.

Personally this update was right up my alley in terms of how I prefer them playing out. I like the comical parts of LIL but it's the triller side that keeps me engaged the most; when shit after shit hits the fan for Sensei and the girls and seeing how they'll deal with whatever new drama's unfolding. Some of the updates are more tame yet still interesting, but this one was by far on of the most interesting.

Of course it's a reset update so that means that we're blessed with another super duper fun reset puzzle that we all enjoy so much! Sarcasm aside, and besides how long it took to get through it despite having a f#&#@$& guide for it, (thanks for those who posted it) it wasn't as bad as it could have been. No stupid questions about bird facts or the volume of the average size bathtub in America. Just had to remember the coffee facts and the numbers for Futaba Rin and Sana, and everything else was late out right in the update. Honestly the reset puzzles would be completely acceptable if they were more like the last happy event with "Amy" in the mall, but whatever.

Also, who bodied Ami?! Like, I knew shit was really gonna start hitting the fan as Chapter 3 concluded, but the way it's happening is very confusing yet interesting. Some are saying that dialogues in this update felt a little flat in areas potentially due to the chapter being wrapped up, but I found that parts of it made up for that with how lively a few of the girls were, specifically Sana, Maya, and Ayane, and especially when Ayana found Ami in the hall. But it begs the question, who why and how? The only thing I can think for now is that Maya it potentially the culprit. She had a motive, and even more so after not only seeing Sensei have sex with Ami while thinking it was her, but having Ami run it in her face as well. Maybe the camel's back broke and that pushed Maya off the deep end. We all know Maya has seen many many horrible things during resets and that she's growed accustomed to them, but maybe the reason behind her "unfazed-ness" was that she had somehow done it, then finally had sex with Sensei herself (again) to go out with a bang.

Then again that's a bit of a stretch (but not much sense it makes the most sense since the only other possibility could be that one of the gods did it, but I can't recall them ever having anything against Ami, unless she's interfering with the whole "take something that doesn't belong to you" thingy.) since Maya was with everyone else when it happened and was shocked that she didn't sense the reset starting, so I don't know if it's possible that it was all a calculated event on her part. Then again, once the reset started Maya and Ayane's behaviors shifted for a while as if they were now ignorant of the resets, just to shift back into the knowledgeable gear out of nowhere, and you can't trust anything once resets start so who really knows. Whatever; 8/10 update. Would be 9 if not for the super fun puzzle. Still a really good update and end of Chapter 3 in my opinion.

No stupid questions about bird facts or the volume of the average size bathtub in America. Just had to remember the coffee facts and the numbers for Futaba Rin and Sana, and everything else was late out right in the update. Honestly the reset puzzles would be completely acceptable if they were more like the last happy event with "Amy" in the mall, but whatever.
Also, who bodied Ami?! Like, I knew shit was really gonna start hitting the fan as Chapter 3 concluded, but the way it's happening is very confusing yet interesting. Some are saying that dialogues in this update felt a little flat in areas potentially due to the chapter being wrapped up, but I found that parts of it made up for that with how lively a few of the girls were, specifically Sana, Maya, and Ayane, and especially when Ayana found Ami in the hall. But it begs the question, who why and how? The only thing I can think for now is that Maya it potentially the culprit. She had a motive, and even more so after not only seeing Sensei have sex with Ami while thinking it was her, but having Ami run it in her face as well. Maybe the camel's back broke and that pushed Maya off the deep end. We all know Maya has seen many many horrible things during resets and that she's growed accustomed to them, but maybe the reason behind her "unfazed-ness" was that she had somehow done it, then finally had sex with Sensei herself (again) to go out with a bang.
Then again that's a bit of a stretch (but not much sense it makes the most sense since the only other possibility could be that one of the gods did it, but I can't recall them ever having anything against Ami, unless she's interfering with the whole "take something that doesn't belong to you" thingy.) since Maya was with everyone else when it happened and was shocked that she didn't sense the reset starting, so I don't know if it's possible that it was all a calculated event on her part. Then again, once the reset started Maya and Ayane's behaviors shifted for a while as if they were now ignorant of the resets, just to shift back into the knowledgeable gear out of nowhere, and you can't trust anything once resets start so who really knows. Whatever; 8/10 update. Would be 9 if not for the super fun puzzle. Still a really good update and end of Chapter 3 in my opinion.

Start felt a bit weak, as others pointed out, it's as if Sel wanted to close all the open matters before finishing the chapter: Otoha & Niki, Imai, Miku, Makoto, Noriko etc. All of their parts felt a bit rushed to get them out of the way before the grand climax.

The obligatory reset puzzle was exactly like how obligatory reset puzzles are: all easy until you remain with the parts you don't get and then it becomes extremely annoying. Reset happy events are the best imo because they show stuff that goes beyond the reset, like Baby Finches and Mother's Milk, but this one had nothing of that. I liked the easter egg where you get a game over screen for getting caught by Kaori and Nao for stealing shampoo

As for the ending, well, we knew it was coming, but it still hurts. Poor Maya

Maya has been worried about her own reset coming for a while now. She was taunted by the angels about it during the first dorm war, then before the end of chapter 2 she had warned Sensei that it might happen, and almost DID happen but he managed to prevent it. That's what we see. Ayane mentions that she'd been hearing the voices from the gods as well, which probably also means that Maya had as well -- stuff we hadn't seen. But the fact that Sensei was dropping REALLY BIG hints that he felt a reset coming, Maya was convinced one wasn't. Which is a pretty clear indicator that their roles in the grand scheme of things has flipped -- he's now the one who senses the resets coming, and she's the one perpetually at risk of erasure.

And if she's truly experienced lifetimes beyond comprehension, to the point where she's lost nearly all enthusiasm for just about anything, perhaps she saw an end, a chance for sweeet oblivion.

Or perhaps she felt her fate was inevitable.

Or perhaps one of the powers that be told her flat out -- he had a task he needed to perform, he failed, and she was to be taken from him as punishment, and this was their last night together so she might as well enjoy it.

But I think most likely, the simplest answer is the correct one -- Sensei never left the room. Neither the Ayane nor the Maya scenes are real, they're all hallucinations, and when we return in January, we'll still be in the room.
